PullRequest.Title: sessions: Support Dev Containers on SSH and Tunnel hosts
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Allow Agents Window sessions to run in Dev Containers on SSH and Tunnel hosts, using the same workspace-mode picker and session handoff as local Dev Containers.

- Run the bundled Dev Container CLI on the source host and carry the container Agent Host protocol through the existing SSH/Tunnel connection using capability-gated extension RPCs.
- Share draft/session preparation, trust checks, configuration/model/agent carryover, worktree lifecycle, rollback, and reconnect behavior between local and remote source providers.
- Preserve source-host identity in persisted container providers and Open in VS Code routing. Keep old hosts and unsupported/nested sources from offering container execution.
- Add SSH ProxyCommand support, standard initial `none` authentication, and known-hosts path handling needed for Docker Sandbox SSH connections.
- Include the generated connection token in standalone dev-host startup URLs so SSH command overrides work without disabling authentication; persistent log URLs remain token-free.
- Add actual Agents Window UI smoke tests for SSH and opt-in real private Tunnels, with isolated hosts/authentication and mock model traffic. Fix raw SSH identity classification and nested workspace submenus exposed by these tests.
- Address both review findings: await provider-started source connections and keep stale failures from disconnecting a replacement attempt.

Uses the existing `chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled` setting. Remote source hosts must run a version advertising the new Dev Container capability. The remote server package now includes `@devcontainers/cli`.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed, zero compilation errors.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, scoped hygiene/ESLint, and diff whitespace checks — passed.
- Affected protocol/provider/picker suites — 811 passing, 11 pending; SSH compatibility suites — 176 passing.
- Follow-up widget/configuration/picker regressions — 223 passing; connection readiness/ownership suites — 29 passing.
- Smoke/automation compilation and hygiene — passed.
- **Actual UI smoke run:** local, SSH, and Tunnel Dev Container suites passed together (3 tests). Each remote case has consecutive successful local UI runs. Tests drive host connection, remote folder selection, Use Dev Container, prompt submission, the rendered response, and session reopening, and verify the outer transport and nested container routing.
- Separate live backend tests also verified Docker Sandbox SSH bootstrap and container session recovery after reconnect over localhost SSH and the real Dev Tunnels relay.
- Test tunnels, containers, processes, and temporary credentials were cleaned up; captured smoke logs were checked for real account-token leakage.

## Smoke test prerequisites

The new remote UI smoke cases live in `test/smoke/src/areas/agentsWindow/agentsWindow.test.ts`; instructions are in `test/smoke/README.md`.

- SSH uses a self-contained loopback SSH fixture and runs with Docker on Linux CI and supported local macOS/Linux machines.
- The real Tunnel case is opt-in via `VSCODE_SMOKE_TEST_TUNNEL_TOKEN`, with a compatible CLI and existing/explicit license consent. It does not require or consume account credentials in ordinary PR smoke jobs.
- Source-mode Tunnel tests use an isolated source-app snapshot to supply the missing Code OSS tunnel-authentication metadata; they do not modify shared product files. Packaged runs require the supplied build's tunnel configuration.
- Both use mock model responses, not paid model requests.

The new UI cases have been exercised locally on macOS. Linux CI also ran and passed the SSH Dev Container UI smoke test; the real Tunnel case was skipped as intended without opt-in credentials. All 33 substantive CI checks passed on `2d68a777eeb`. This PR remains a draft and requires one collaborator approval.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed event source, repeated connection-state emissions, global cache clear, two-per-workspace filesystem boundary, limiter, and picker-visible refresh path are all directly traced in repository code. Exact recent counts and filesystem/network latency vary, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem existence checks and remote Agent Host RPC calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each connection-state event invalidates availability for every cached recent workspace; rebuilding the visible picker performs two fileService.exists calls per effective local or connected-remote recent, with up to four probes concurrently, and configured workspaces also issue an isDockerAvailable RPC. Cost grows with recent-workspace count and repeats across connecting, connected, reconnecting, and disconnected transitions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive filesystem/remote I/O and delayed Dev Container mode decoration while connecting or reconnecting hosts
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this added listener, the Dev Container availability event fired only when the connector was registered or removed, so the workspace picker retained its per-provider/per-folder cache across unrelated remote connection changes.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every IRemoteAgentHostService connection change now emits one global Dev Container availability event. Each initialized provider re-emits it, and WorkspacePicker responds by clearing its entire availability map and limiter before re-probing all visible recent workspaces.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 185 newly registers `this._remoteAgentHostService.onDidChangeConnections(() => this._onDidChangeAvailability.fire())`, converting every generic remote connection transition into a global availability-cache invalidation; no equivalent connection-driven invalidation existed before the diff.
Findings.Title: Scope Dev Container availability invalidation to the changed host
Findings.Impact: Opening the workspace picker while connecting or reconnecting an SSH/Tunnel host causes all local and other-host Dev Container availability entries to be discarded and probed again. RemoteAgentHostService emits at least once before connect and again after connect, so a normal host connection can repeat the full cold probe and generate 2N filesystem calls for N recents per transition, plus Docker RPCs for configured folders.
Findings.Evidence: The added line forwards every onDidChangeConnections event without identifying the affected address or checking whether Dev Container capability changed. RemoteAgentHostService fires this event before client.connect(), after successful connection, and on reconnect state changes. WorkspacePicker subscribes to each provider's onDidChangeDevContainerAvailability and calls _clearDevContainerAvailability(true), which clears the global cache/limiter; rebuilding invokes _isDevContainerWorkspaceAvailable for each recent. The connector's hasDevContainerConfiguration uses Promise.all over two fileService.exists calls, and then calls mainService.isDockerAvailable for matching folders.
Findings.Recommendation: Track the availability signature per SSH/Tunnel address and emit only when that host's connected/capability state changes, carrying the affected provider/address so WorkspacePicker invalidates only matching cache keys. Preserve the existing global invalidation only for connector registration/removal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the workspace picker while an SSH/Tunnel host connects or reconnects
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker renders immediately, but Dev Container mode actions wait for availability probes; remote connection transitions synchronously clear the cache and schedule another visible-picker refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two calls per effective recent workspace on every cold or invalidated availability pass; remote URIs traverse the Agent Host filesystem provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Remote recent workspaces were not probed, and generic remote connection transitions did not invalidate the existing local per-folder cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Controls when the picker can expose the Use Dev Container submenu; repeated waves also consume local/remote I/O while the connection workflow is active.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request host-side Docker availability through the Agent Host extension RPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC for each invalidated workspace whose Dev Container configuration exists; the underlying host executable lookup is cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only local workspaces used the shared-process service; remote hosts had no availability RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the mode action appears.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective local and connected-remote recent workspaces shown by the active picker tab after deduplication; each cold entry probes two configuration paths, with configured entries adding one Docker-availability RPC.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A global Limiter bounds availability checks to four workspaces, while each workspace issues its two file-existence checks in parallel. Connection transitions can initiate repeated waves after the 50 ms refresh scheduler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: WorkspacePicker normally caches by provider and folder across opens. The added global connection listener clears every key on each generic connection transition; host-side Docker discovery itself is promise-cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new global event, picker-wide cache clear, limiter, and two-per-workspace boundary are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of visible recents and remote filesystem latency vary, but a normal connection emits at least connecting and connected events, so repeated invalidation is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium boundary fan-out: one host transition defeats unrelated warm cache entries and repeats collection-wide filesystem/RPC work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Establish a direct or ProxyCommand SSH Agent Host connection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration resolution now completes before socket connection; host-key verification, authentication, endpoint discovery, and the SSH network handshake then follow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per host per ten-second cold window; subsequent setup and known-host lookup reuse the promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The service already used `ssh -G` for known-host lookup; the diff moves/reuses its result earlier so resolved host, identity, and ProxyCommand settings are available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Now precedes opening the SSH socket and can delay connect by up to its five-second timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat candidate known-host paths to recover unquoted spaces
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typical absolute/home-separated lists require roughly one stat per path; a segment of T whitespace tokens can generate T(T+1)/2 candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Parsing was CPU-only and did not stat candidate paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs inside cold `ssh -G` resolution before connect.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch and own configured SSH ProxyCommand
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one process for a connection that has ProxyCommand; none for ordinary direct SSH.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Configured ProxyCommand was ignored and no proxy process was launched.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provides the SSH socket and remains live for the connection lifetime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SSH handshake and Agent Host transport
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One live SSH client per connection attempt, with existing reconnect policy.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected host, with known-host path token count controlling filesystem probes; reconnects within ten seconds reuse successful resolution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One `ssh -G` subprocess per cold host resolution. User/global path lists resolve in parallel, while candidate stats within each list are sequential. One ProxyCommand subprocess exists only when configured.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful `ssh -G` resolution is coalesced and reused per host for ten seconds; failures are immediately evicted. Known-host file contents follow existing handling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary placement and cardinality; low prevalence for pathological candidate counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Path lists with many whitespace tokens or slow network-mounted homes can cost more, but normal OpenSSH defaults and Docker Sandbox paths are short and the result is cached.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: proxy lifetime is cleaned up, config work is coalesced, and normal path cardinality is too small to establish a realistic regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or restore a Dev Container session on an SSH/Tunnel source host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve or connect the source host, request workspace trust, run Dev Container setup, locate/install the remote CLI, start/reuse the container Agent Host, create the relay, then initialize the nested session provider.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect/reconnect the SSH or Tunnel source Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when warm; otherwise one provider/service-started connection wait for the source address.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only desktop-local source workspaces were supported.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before remote Docker or container commands can run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request source workspace trust and Dev Container lifecycle methods over the parent Agent Host protocol
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One trust request and one connect request per launch; disconnect and relay calls follow lifecycle/traffic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Local Dev Container service calls stayed in desktop/shared-process IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Trust and connect responses are on the launch critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run Dev Container CLI `up`, bounded setup/inspection exec commands, and the relay process on the source host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `up` per launch attempt plus a bounded sequence of setup/platform/endpoint commands and one relay; not multiplied by session history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent work existed for local source folders; the diff enables it on the remote source host.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download/install matching remote CLI when absent
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold installation only; reused once installed in the container.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing local Dev Container launch had the same cold installation step.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the cold startup critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected source workspace. The service coalesces concurrent connection requests by workspace key; setup command count is bounded rather than per session-history item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pending container launch per workspace. Platform probes run three commands concurrently; most setup/installation phases are serialized. Relay reconnect creates one replacement connection at a time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Source connection and pending container connection are reused/coalesced; Docker executable discovery and shell environment are promise-cached. Persisted providers restore metadata without eagerly starting containers. Cold CLI/container setup remains expensive; warm runs can reuse installation and endpoint state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: active/pending maps, cancellation tokens, and tests establish coalescing and late cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Container image state, CLI installation state, and SSH/Tunnel latency dominate duration, but multiplicity and ownership are bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No further finding: the heavyweight boundaries are inherent to the newly supported workflow and are coalesced per workspace with explicit cancellation/cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Exchange nested Agent Host protocol traffic and recover after parent transport loss
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each client-to-container frame is serialized and sent through the parent extension request; server-to-client frames arrive as notifications. Parent loss closes owned IDs and the nested transport establishes one replacement relay.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON stringify/parse nested AHP frames and wrap them in parent JSON-RPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One wrapper request or notification per protocol frame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Local containers crossed shared-process IPC; remote containers did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly carries live session traffic; no extra collection-wide work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send relay frames over the existing SSH/Tunnel Agent Host transport
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One parent request per outbound nested frame and one notification per inbound frame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required transport path for remote container sessions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Protocol frame rate and number of simultaneously active remote container connections on one parent host.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Outbound extension requests are fire-and-forget from RelayTransport and may overlap; reconnect establishment is sequenced by the reconnecting transport. Listener fan-out grows with active connections/clients but ordinary ownership is small.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No frame cache or batching; connection maps filter routing by generated ID. Reconnection reuses the facade but creates a fresh relay ID.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for per-frame wrapping, insufficient evidence that realistic traffic creates a user-visible burst or retained pending-request regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frame rates under terminal-heavy or highly streaming workloads are not established by the diff or tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: per-frame relay overhead is required by the feature, and the reviewed evidence does not establish realistic harmful concurrency or retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconcile, archive, or delete detached worktrees owned by a remote source host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A successful container session listing derives active handles, resolves the source connection, then sends one reconciliation RPC; archive/delete similarly resolve once and send one RPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconnect the source SSH/Tunnel host if absent
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one source connection attempt per operation when cold, normally zero while the container relay's parent is live.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Container worktree lifecycle always targeted the local Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before remote worktree lifecycle RPCs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconcile one collection of handles or mutate one handle
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reconciliation RPC per latest successful listing; one archive/delete RPC per user operation, with duplicate deletes coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same logical RPCs targeted the local Agent Host without remote connection resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reconciliation is background; archive/delete await completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of retained session handles is serialized in one reconciliation request; delete tasks are coalesced per handle.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reconciliations can overlap while source resolution is pending, but only the latest proceeds to RPC. Different handle deletions may run independently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm source connections are reused. A generation counter suppresses stale reconciliation after a newer listing; deletion promises coalesce duplicate handle cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for generation and per-handle coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency depends on session refresh and user lifecycle actions, but stale passes are explicitly suppressed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added remote boundary is necessary and latest-only reconciliation prevents stale fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: List and delete Dev Tunnels with an explicitly selected authentication provider
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Acquire the selected provider token, issue one tunnel list; deletion issues one delete followed by one refresh list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List tunnels, or delete one tunnel and refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list for discovery; delete workflow remains one delete plus one list refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same boundary count, but token acquisition could use a previously cached provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Interactive tunnel picker waits for these operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tunnel collection returned by the service; the diff does not add per-tunnel network calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations remain serialized by the interactive picker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider selection may be cached, but an explicit provider now overrides it. Service/SDK tunnel caches otherwise retain prior behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network latency varies but call cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; authentication provider routing changes without increasing boundary count.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The remote server artifact must be downloaded and unpacked before the host starts; the newly declared Dev Containers CLI dependency is included in that package.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One artifact transfer per uncached remote server version.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The remote artifact did not declare this dependency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Potentially affects cold remote installation only, not warm startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One package installation per server version/remote target, independent of workspace or session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Package download/unpack follows existing remote installation behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal remote-server version caching avoids repeat installation for the same build; no runtime eager launch of the CLI was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the dependency is added; insufficient evidence of an actionable packaging regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The diff does not provide packaged size delta or measurements, so concrete latency impact is unproven.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding because package-size/performance impact is not quantified and the dependency directly supplies the advertised host capability.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 70 changed files and every paginated diff hunk. Traced picker availability, SSH configuration/proxy setup, remote Dev Container launch/relay/reconnect, worktree lifecycle, tunnel discovery, UI-only routing, and remote packaging. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity finding for global cache invalidation causing repeated collection-wide filesystem/RPC probes; other expensive boundaries were bounded, cached/coalesced, required by the new workflow, or lacked evidence of realistic harmful magnitude.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
